title: Makefile: make docs target work with BSD and GNU tools
body:
macOS ships with BSD sed, BSD grep and a version of man that does not support -L. Give it the same treatment as FreeBSD to avoid warnings during the build and potentially incorrect output.

comments.body: Seems like the [ci / sys remote root fedora-rawhide / lima (pull_request)](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/actions/runs/37285300120/job/111689604144?pr=29900) job timed out? This change doesn't affect Fedora, so I don't think this is related.
It is flaky. I rettrigrer CI.

No, these tools aren't included by default. I think it's better to throw an error saying `ggrep` isn't installed rather than failing on non-existent flags. I lost hours debugging a similar issue when I first switched to macOS.

> No, these tools aren't included by default. I think it's better to throw an error saying ggrep isn't installed rather than failing on non-existent flags. I lost hours debugging a similar issue when I first switched to macOS.

Is that really better than the current behavior though? An error message on a missing flag vs missing command but both of those lead to a passing job. Also if I'm not wrong, with this change, we might be generating empty man pages given we don't have `gsed` installed on the runners.

We should fail explicitly (perhaps using a check tools target as a prerequisite) _and_ maybe also install these tools on the runners?

> Is that really better than the current behavior though? An error message on a missing flag vs missing command but both of those lead to a passing job.

Yeah, I'd say that's a bug. It should never have passed in the first place, e.g., by setting the `-o pipefail` option of bash and failing the entire pipeline.

> Also if I'm not wrong, with this change, we might be generating empty man pages given we don't have `gsed` installed on the runners.

Yes. Previously they were subtly different from what you had expected. I'd rather take the obvious failure rather than the quiet one.

> We should fail explicitly (perhaps using a check tools target as a prerequisite) _and_ maybe also install these tools on the runners?

Yes.

Well I rather avoid having to tell each macos contributor to install the GNU tools as well.

If we validate that in an extra target we could make this part of validate job which just runs on linux and then do not have to make then run on macos or other targets
